value.rationale: The minority jamming coverage curvature is directly motivated as an unresolved quantitative feature in the source paper, rather than an arbitrary statistic. The exact second-order coefficient identifies physically meaningful late minor-species depositions following majority-species rejection and distinguishes the repeated-attempt process from a simplified two-attempt process. This supplies a size-independent finite-volume benchmark for rare-species adsorption; no macroscopic limiting theorem is asserted.
